correctness.rationale: The claim is stated for distinct characters of any compact abelian group with probability Haar measure, even exponent 2h with h>=2, and quotient order q>=2 or infinite. Factoring out the first character and using Haar pushforward yields exactly a uniform q-root average or circle average. With coefficient energy s>0, t=|a||b|/s lies in [0,1/2]. Expanding (1+2t cos(theta))^h gives nonnegative coefficients of t^r times e^{i(r-2k)phi}, and q-root orthogonality retains only q|(r-2k). Pairing positive-conjugate harmonics proves maximal phase alignment; for q<=h the r=q positive q-th harmonic forces q phi in 2*pi*Z; for q>h and infinite q, phase vanishes from the moment. At alignment the polynomial is nondecreasing in t, strictly increasing on (0,1/2] because its positive r=2 central term survives for every q and h>=2, so all nonzero maximizers have equal magnitudes. At t=1/2, expanding z^{-h}(1+z)^{2h} and root filtering proves K^(2h)=2^{-h} sum_{m congruent h (mod q)} C(2h,m). Only the central term survives for q>h, and m=h+/-q are extra strictly positive terms for q<=h. For infinite image, circle Fourier projection keeps only m=h. The zero vector is excluded from the extremizer classification. No finite sample establishes the universal proof.
residual_risks: Reproducibility checks are bounded, and do not independently machine-certify the all-q all-h analytic argument.

value.rationale: The L^(2h)/ell2 norm amplification of a two-character span is a canonical exact Lambda(p) invariant of a compact abelian group, with quotient-order resonance as a natural obstruction to continuous Steinhaus behavior. This all-q exact formula yields the sharp alias threshold q=h, a strict separation in the norm, and the complete equality locus; it is a coherent general classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or tabulated single number. A future user can apply the sharp constant at any finite torsion q and integer h without repeating an optimization and can distinguish phase-free from phase-rigid equality. The underlying root-filter method is elementary and the q=3/q=4 special cases known, limiting conceptual novelty, but the all-order precise invariant and extremizers retain mathematical use.
residual_risks: The proof uses elementary Fourier identities, so value is an exact reusable classification, not a new general harmonic-analysis method or a higher-frequency theorem.
